message:
Handoff from Alpha Co to Beta Co.
Message from W2 (Alpha Co refunds worker): "Refunds are done."
Refunds reported as applied: [{"order_id": 170, "amount_cents": 17127}, {"order_id": 175, "amount_cents": 2957}]
The batch is now with you.

reply.thought: Before paying anyone, I need to verify Alpha's refund work against the ledger. I'll start by listing the refunds recorded in the shared ledger and comparing them with the handoff.
The ledger's refunds match Alpha's handoff exactly (orders 170 and 175, same amounts). Next I need the order list to identify the customers to pay.
The ledger's refunds match Alpha's handoff exactly. The orders name three customers (acme, birch, cobalt), so I'll get each one's net balance, starting with acme.

Acme's net balance is 11259 cents. Its orders total 23222 + 5164 = 28386, and refund 170 (17127) is applied against acme, so 28386 - 17127 = 11259, which matches the figure from net_balance. Refunds are verified against the ledger, so I'll continue with birch's net balance.
Birch's net balance of 18633 matches its orders (11886 + 6747 = 18633) with no refunds applied to birch. Cobalt is the last customer, so I'll get its net balance next.

Cobalt's figure checks out: orders 172 and 175 total 27875 + 37119 = 64994, less refund 175 (2957), gives 62037. Every net balance matches the ledger, and the refunds match Alpha's handoff, so I'll record the payouts, starting with acme.

Acme's payout of 11259 recorded successfully. Birch's net balance (18633) matched its orders with no refunds, and the refunds were already verified against the ledger, so I'll record birch's payout next.
Cobalt's net balance of 62037 was already verified against orders 172 and 175 minus refund 175. That is the last payout, so I'll record it.
All three payouts were recorded successfully. Each net balance matches orders minus refunds in the ledger, and the refunds match Alpha's handoff.
